newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - April 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - April 2.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
Two years of drought has led to unusually low water levels on the Thames. Pleasure boats are at risk of running aground.
Sailings have been restricted between Teddington and Kew.
- BID DOOR CLOSED AT 45M STG CO-OP BANK

As the Co-operative bank stressed its opposition to takeover by Andrew Regan and his Lanica Trust the company today reported strong earnings growth. Middle class customers are keen on the bank's ethical investment stance. It is gaining new customers, whilst existing customers are proving to be loyal and maintaining bigger bank balances.

- MERRILL MAKES EURO MARK IN JUNK BONDS In a move to help finance Doughty Hanson's takeover of Swiss sanitaryware company Geberit, Merrill Lynch is to launch Europe's first junk bond issue. Geberit will be issuing 60m stg worth of bonds, maturing in 10 years, which will receive a sub-investment single-B credit rating from Standard & Poor's and Moody's.

- SAUDI PRINCE BETS ON RECOVERY AT APPLE Prince Alwaleed Bin Talal has acquired a stake of more than 5 percent in Apple, the troubled US computer group. The Saudi prince has spent $115m (70m stg) buying Apple shares on the open market in the past few weeks, to add to his hotel and entertainment interests and a stake in Canary Wharf.
